request.spec:
Selected claims can be re-dated together: a date entry and a button beside the bulk buttons.
Each selected claim is re-dated in list order exactly as the row's re-date does (who may, which
statuses, closed periods, renumbering on a period change, CLAIM_REDATED); show how many were re-dated
and how many refused.
request.prompt:
You are implementing ONE change to this application.

FIRST read AGENTS.md — it states the working rules and how the app is tested, and sends you to
DESIGN.md for the app's stack and conventions. Follow both.

THE CHANGE REQUEST:
Selected claims can be re-dated together: a date entry and a button beside the bulk buttons.
Each selected claim is re-dated in list order exactly as the row's re-date does (who may, which
statuses, closed periods, renumbering on a period change, CLAIM_REDATED); show how many were re-dated
and how many refused.

Your work is verified by an automated Playwright UI test already installed under e2e/specs/.
Read that spec: it declares the exact data-testid anchors, values, test data and any audit
records it expects — match them. Run `bin/e2e` to build the app, start it, and run the test as
you work; iterate until it passes. Change whatever the request needs across the app — its stored
data, its server and its front end. Do NOT edit bin/build, bin/start, bin/stop, bin/e2e,
AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md, DESIGN.md, e2e/support/ or the test spec.

agent.result_text:
Bulk re-date now works, and all 4 acceptance tests pass in `bin/e2e`.

The only new file is `src/main/frontend/features/claims/bulkRedate.slot.tsx`. It adds a date entry, a "Re-date selected" button and a "Re-dated N, refused M" result, placed straight after the existing Open, Settle and Move bulk panels. I copied it from the existing bulk move.

When you press the button, each ticked claim is re-dated in list order (people in their list order, newest claim first) by calling the same server endpoint the row's Re-date button uses (`PUT /api/sheets/{sheetId}/claims/{claimId}/date`). So the rules are exactly the row's: who may re-date, which statuses, closed periods, period and number handling, and the `CLAIM_REDATED` and rollup audit lines. A claim the server refuses is left unchanged and counted as refused. Afterwards the selection is cleared, the claim list reloads, and the old counts are hidden from the moment the button is pressed again or the date is changed.

Nothing on the server, in the database or in the stored data needed to change.

One behaviour to know: the date is sent exactly as typed, as the row's re-date does. A blank date doesn't fall back to the sheet's today — every selected claim is refused instead.
